summary: Swami Sivananda Saraswati worked in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology, studying at Thanjavur Medical College circa 1905–1910. He founded the Divine Life Society in 1936 and the Yoga-Vedanta Forest Academy in 1948, teaching Xiangguang Zhou and Boris Sacharow.
Active in religious studies and philosophy, Swami Vimalananda studied at Ripon College. In 1897, he became a disciple and student of Swami Vivekananda.

Swami Vivekananda was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Presidency University, Scottish Church College, and the University of Calcutta between 1879 and 1884, and studied under Ramakrishna circa 1881–1886.
Sydney Frank Markham was active in history and archaeology, having studied at Wadham College circa 1920–1924. He served at the Museums Association circa 1928–1942 as Secretary and later President.

Syed Ali Bilgrami worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at Patna College, IIT Roorkee, Royal School of Mines, and the universities of Lucknow and London. He served the Government of Hyderabad (~1879–1901) and became Reader in Marathi at Cambridge in 1901.

Syed Ameer Ali worked in history, archaeology, and religious studies. He studied at Aliah University and the University of Calcutta (circa 1863–1869), later holding a post at the University of Calcutta circa 1878–1881.

Historian and Indologist Syed Hasan Askari studied at Zila School Chapra, Langat Singh College (~1920–1922), and Patna University (~1922–1924). He served as Director of the K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute from 1968 to 1971, succeeding Anant Sadashiv Altekar.
Syed Nawab Ali was a scholar of history and archaeology. In 1932, he was attested as Professor of Persian at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda and as Principal of Bahauddin College.

Sylvain Brocquet, an Indologist and linguist, studied at École Normale Supérieure (1980) and under Marie-Claude Porcher (~1990–1997). He held a post at Aix-Marseille University circa 2000 and taught Perrine Estienne-Monod.

Sylvain Lévi studied at the Sorbonne under Abel Bergaigne. A specialist in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, he held posts at the EPHE, University of Paris, Collège de France (1890–1935), Visva-Bharati University, and Maison Franco-Japonaise.
Specializing in Buddhist studies and sinology, Sze-bong Tso completed a PhD at the Australian National University (1977–1982) under the supervision of Jan Willem de Jong and Tissa Rajapatirana.
Indologist Søren Sørensen held posts at the Herlufsholm School from 1876 to 1878 and at the University of Copenhagen circa 1887–1902.
Sāmaṇera Bodhesako worked in Buddhist studies. He founded Path Press and served as an editor at the Buddhist Publication Society.
Sīlaratano studied under Narada Maha Thera, Nyanaponika Thera, and Ajahn Maha Bua (~1977–2011).

Sōkō Morinaga, a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar, studied at Toyama High School, Daitoku-ji, and under Zuigan Goto and Sessō Oda. He served as head of Hanazono University (1986–1994) and abbot (住職) at Daiju-in (1963–1995).

Specializing in Indology, history, and archaeology, T. A. Gopinatha Rao served as Tamil Assistant at the Archaeological Survey of India (~1901–1908) and as Superintendent of Archæology for the Travancore State Department of Archaeology (~1908–1919).

Indologist T. Chandrasekharan studied under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. Attested in 1951, he succeeded T. R. Chintamani as Professor of History of Sanskrit Language and Literature at Madras Sanskrit College.

Indologist T. Ganapati Sastri earned a PhD from the University of Tübingen. From circa 1908 to 1926, he served as Curator at the Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library and as Editor of the Trivandrum Sanskrit Series.

T. Griffith Foulk studied at the University of Michigan (PhD attested 1987) under Luis Oscar Gómez. Focusing on Buddhist studies, Japanology, and Sinology, he taught at Michigan (~1987–1995) and Sarah Lawrence College, where he was Riggs Professor of Religion (attested 2015).

Working in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy, T. K. V. Desikachar studied under Tirumalai Krishnamacharya from circa 1961 to 1989. He founded the Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram in 1976 and taught Raghu Ananthanarayanan.
